es: Reconocer peticiones muy indirectas (I don't suppose you could, would it be at all possible, I was wondering if) y elegir el grado de indirección que pide cada situación.

vocabulary.es: por si acaso, por si hay suerte

teaching.en: I don't suppose you could lend me your ladder for the weekend, could you? I would hate to impose, but mine has just broken.
teaching.es: No creo que pudieras prestarme tu escalera para el fin de semana, ¿verdad? Odiaría molestar, pero la mía acaba de romperse.
teaching.explanationEs: I don't suppose you could + verbo base espera un «no»; hate to impose reconoce que estás pidiendo una carga.
segments: I don't suppose you could lend me your ladder for the weekend,
could you? I would hate to impose, but mine has just broken.
teaching.audioText: I don't suppose you could lend me your ladder for the weekend, could you? I would hate to impose, but mine has just broken.

teaching.en: Would it be at all possible to borrow the ladder until Sunday afternoon, if that would not be too much trouble for you?
teaching.es: ¿Sería posible en absoluto pedir prestada la escalera hasta el domingo por la tarde, si no es demasiada molestia para ti?
teaching.explanationEs: Would it be (at all) possible to + verbo: muy formal; at all suaviza todavía más.
segments: Would it be at all possible to borrow the ladder until Sunday
afternoon, if that would not be too much trouble for you?
teaching.audioText: Would it be at all possible to borrow the ladder until Sunday afternoon, if that would not be too much trouble for you?

teaching.en: I was wondering if you might do me a favour, by any chance, because I cannot reach the top shelf without something to stand on.
teaching.es: Me preguntaba si por casualidad podrías hacerme un favor, porque no llego al estante de arriba sin algo donde subirme.
teaching.explanationEs: I was wondering if + might/could: el pasado crea distancia; by any chance añade cautela.
segments: I was wondering if you might do me a favour, by any chance,
because I cannot reach the top shelf without something to stand on.
teaching.audioText: I was wondering if you might do me a favour, by any chance, because I cannot reach the top shelf without something to stand on.

teaching.en: Would you mind lending me the ladder for an hour? I'm only asking on the off chance that you are not using it today.
teaching.es: ¿Te importaría prestarme la escalera una hora? Solo te lo pido por si acaso no la estás usando hoy.
teaching.explanationEs: Would you mind + verbo en -ing; on the off chance that = por si hay suerte, sin esperar un sí.
segments: Would you mind lending me the ladder for an hour? I'm only
asking on the off chance that you are not using it today.
teaching.audioText: Would you mind lending me the ladder for an hour? I'm only asking on the off chance that you are not using it today.

teaching.en: Our neighbour is very polite, so she never says «Lend me the ladder»; she softens every request and leaves us an easy way to refuse.
teaching.es: Nuestra vecina es muy educada, así que nunca dice «Préstame la escalera»; suaviza cada petición y nos deja una salida fácil para negarnos.
teaching.explanationEs: Una orden directa solo encaja entre amigos muy cercanos; la cortesía consiste en dejar una salida.
segments: Our neighbour is very polite, so she never says «Lend me the ladder»;
she softens every request and leaves us an easy way to refuse.
teaching.audioText: Our neighbour is very polite, so she never says «Lend me the ladder»; she softens every request and leaves us an easy way to refuse.

teaching.en: The bigger the favour, or the greater the distance between you and your neighbour, the more polite and indirect the request should be.
teaching.es: Cuanto mayor es el favor, o la distancia entre tú y tu vecino, más cortés e indirecta debe ser la petición.
teaching.explanationEs: The + comparativo… the + comparativo; con un amigo basta un simple Could you…?
segments: The bigger the favour, or the greater the distance between you and
your neighbour, the more polite and indirect the request should be.
teaching.audioText: The bigger the favour, or the greater the distance between you and your neighbour, the more polite and indirect the request should be.

prompt.es: Elige la petición más indirecta y adecuada para la vecina cansada.

choices.text: Can you lend me your ladder for a few hours this afternoon, please? Thanks a lot.
I don't suppose you could lend me your ladder for a few hours, could you?
Lend me your ladder for a few hours this afternoon, if you don't mind, please.

feedback.es: Con alguien a quien apenas conoces y un favor molesto, el grado máximo de indirección deja una salida fácil.

hint.es: Busca la fórmula que empieza con I don't suppose y lleva could.

origin.text: Your neighbour has just come back from a long trip, and you hardly know her. You need to borrow her ladder for a few hours this afternoon.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Sería posible en absoluto pedir prestada tu escalera hasta el domingo?»

feedback.es: Would it be at all possible to… es la fórmula más formal para pedir algo que puede molestar.

origin.text: I am so sorry to ask, but would it be at all ___ to borrow your ladder until Sunday? I can bring it back early.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Te importaría prestarme la escalera una hora?»

answer.text: Would you mind lending me the ladder for an hour

feedback.es: Would you mind va seguido de un verbo en -ing: lending, no to lend.

hint.es: Empieza por Would you mind y usa el verbo en -ing.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada petición con su grado de indirección.

pairs: Could you lend me the keys?
I was wondering if you might lend me the keys.
I don't suppose you could lend me the keys.

feedback.es: El grado sube con cada capa de cortesía: orden, pregunta neutra, pasado de cortesía y fórmula que espera un no.

pairs: Could you lend me the keys?
I was wondering if you might lend me the keys.
I don't suppose you could lend me the keys.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué el narrador ensayó tanto su petición.

choices.text: The neighbour had already refused to lend him the ladder once before.
He wanted to agree a price for borrowing the ladder first of all.
He hardly knew his neighbour and did not want to impose.

feedback.es: Apenas conocía a su vecino: ensayó para no parecer insistente ni abusar con un favor a un casi desconocido.

origin.audio: When I moved into my new flat, I needed a ladder to reach the ceiling, and the only person who had one was my neighbour, Mr Hill, whom I hardly knew. I practised the request all morning. In the end I went to his door and said: I'm so sorry to bother you, and I hate to impose, but I was wondering if by any chance you might lend me your ladder for ten minutes. He said of course, and told me to keep it until the weekend.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Te importaría vigilar mi bolso un minuto mientras compro un billete?»

feedback.es: Would you mind + -ing es una petición cortés y más indirecta que Could you…?

origin.text: Excuse me, I hate to bother you, but would you ___ watching my bag for a minute while I buy a ticket?

prompt.es: Elige la petición que mejor encaja con la situación de Sara.

choices.text: I don't suppose you could cover my meeting on Friday, could you? I have to leave early.
Could you cover my meeting on Friday, please? I have to leave early for a family event, sorry.
You need to cover my meeting on Friday, because I have to leave early.

feedback.es: Un favor grande, pedido por alguien nuevo a su jefe, exige la fórmula más indirecta: espera un no y deja salida.

origin.text: Sara has worked at the company for only two months. She needs to leave early on Friday for a family event, so her manager, Mr Clark, would have to cover her meeting with a client. It is a big favour.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué da a entender Ana con «please say no if it's a bad time»?

choices.text: She would honestly prefer it if he refused her request.
She wants help but leaves him an easy way out.
She has already asked somebody else to read the report.

feedback.es: Decir «di que no si es mal momento» es cortesía: la petición sigue en pie, pero Tom no queda obligado.

origin.audio: Hi Tom, it's Ana. I don't suppose you could possibly take a look at my report before the meeting tomorrow? I know you're very busy, and there's absolutely no pressure, so please say no if it's a bad time. It's just that I would really like a second opinion.

prompt.es: Completa: «Odio molestarte, pero ¿podrías prestarme el coche una hora?»

feedback.es: I hate to impose prepara al oyente para una petición que supone una carga y reduce la presión.

origin.text: I hate to ___, but I was wondering whether you might lend me your car for an hour. I will fill it up before I bring it back.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Sería posible en absoluto salir un poco antes?»

answer.text: Would it be at all possible to leave a bit earlier

feedback.es: Would it be at all possible to + verbo base encadena la fórmula muy formal con lo que se pide.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué fin añade Leo «I fully understand if this is not possible»?

choices.text: To say that he will hand in the essay on Monday anyway.
To warn the teacher that he is unhappy with the deadline.
To leave the teacher a polite way out of refusing.

feedback.es: La frase final no retira la petición: rebaja la presión y permite a la profesora negarse sin incomodidad.

origin.text: Dear Mrs Rossi, I hope you are well. I was wondering whether it might be possible to move the deadline for my essay to Monday, as I have been ill. I fully understand if this is not possible. Kind regards, Leo

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué pide la hablante y cómo lo pide.

choices.text: She asks for the window to be closed, and gives a reason.
She orders a stranger to close the window and apologises later.
She offers to close the window for someone who feels cold.

feedback.es: La hablante pide cerrar la ventana con Would you mind… y justifica la petición por su hijo, sin imponer nada.

origin.audio: Excuse me, sorry to trouble you, but would you mind closing the window? It has got rather cold in here, and my little boy has only just got over a cough. I wouldn't ask, but I don't want him to catch another cold.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me preguntaba si por casualidad podrías hacerme un favor.»

feedback.es: By any chance añade cautela: sugiere que el favor es improbable o molesto, y suaviza la petición.

origin.text: I was wondering if you might, by any ___, do me a small favour. It should only take five minutes.

es: Sustituir expresiones crudas por eufemismos y atenuaciones (between jobs, passed away, let go, not the best) al hablar de temas delicados.

teaching.en: Saying «unemployed» can feel blunt, so many people prefer the euphemism «between jobs», which suggests that the situation is only temporary.
teaching.es: Decir «unemployed» puede resultar brusco, así que muchos prefieren el eufemismo «between jobs», que sugiere que la situación es solo temporal.
teaching.explanationEs: Between jobs es un eufemismo: suaviza la situación y deja abierta una salida.
segments: Saying «unemployed» can feel blunt, so many people prefer the euphemism
«between jobs», which suggests that the situation is only temporary.
teaching.audioText: Saying «unemployed» can feel blunt, so many people prefer the euphemism «between jobs», which suggests that the situation is only temporary.

teaching.en: When my elderly neighbour passed away last month, the family asked us not to say «died», because «passed away» sounds softer and more respectful.
teaching.es: Cuando mi vecino mayor falleció el mes pasado, la familia nos pidió que no dijéramos «died», porque «passed away» suena más suave y respetuoso.
teaching.explanationEs: Passed away es más suave que died; elderly es más amable que old.
segments: When my elderly neighbour passed away last month, the family asked us
not to say «died», because «passed away» sounds softer and more respectful.
teaching.audioText: When my elderly neighbour passed away last month, the family asked us not to say «died», because «passed away» sounds softer and more respectful.

teaching.en: The company decided to let go of three workers, so the manager spoke gently and explained that the decision was not about their performance.
teaching.es: La empresa decidió prescindir de tres trabajadores, así que la directora habló con delicadeza y explicó que la decisión no dependía de su rendimiento.
teaching.explanationEs: Let go = forma suave de fire; gently describe el tono con que se da la noticia.
segments: The company decided to let go of three workers, so the manager
spoke gently and explained that the decision was not about their performance.
teaching.audioText: The company decided to let go of three workers, so the manager spoke gently and explained that the decision was not about their performance.

teaching.en: Calling a terrible film «not the best» is a classic understatement: the listener understands perfectly that you did not enjoy it at all.
teaching.es: Llamar «not the best» a una película terrible es una atenuación clásica: el oyente entiende perfectamente que no la disfrutaste en absoluto.
teaching.explanationEs: Not the best rebaja la opinión: dice menos de lo que siente, y el oyente entiende «malo».
segments: Calling a terrible film «not the best» is a classic understatement: the
listener understands perfectly that you did not enjoy it at all.
teaching.audioText: Calling a terrible film «not the best» is a classic understatement: the listener understands perfectly that you did not enjoy it at all.

teaching.en: Estate agents often rely on euphemism: «cosy» can mean tiny, and «full of character» can mean that the building needs a lot of repair.
teaching.es: Los agentes inmobiliarios recurren a menudo al eufemismo: «cosy» puede significar diminuto, y «full of character» que el edificio necesita muchas reparaciones.
teaching.explanationEs: Los anuncios de pisos usan eufemismos; el mensaje real es otro.
segments: Estate agents often rely on euphemism: «cosy» can mean tiny, and «full
of character» can mean that the building needs a lot of repair.
teaching.audioText: Estate agents often rely on euphemism: «cosy» can mean tiny, and «full of character» can mean that the building needs a lot of repair.

teaching.en: There is a time to sugarcoat bad news and a time to be direct, so never beat around the bush when someone needs a clear answer.
teaching.es: Hay momentos para endulzar una mala noticia y momentos para ser directo, así que no te andes por las ramas cuando alguien necesita una respuesta clara.
teaching.explanationEs: Sugarcoat = endulzar; beat around the bush = dar rodeos. Elige según la persona y el momento.
segments: There is a time to sugarcoat bad news and a time to be
direct, so never beat around the bush when someone needs a clear answer.
teaching.audioText: There is a time to sugarcoat bad news and a time to be direct, so never beat around the bush when someone needs a clear answer.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que suaviza «The bank fired Sara» al hablar con una amiga.

choices.text: Sara was simply fired from the bank last week.
Sara was kicked out of the bank last week.
Sara was let go by the bank last week.

feedback.es: Let go conserva el significado de fire pero sin crudeza; las otras dos opciones son directas o incluso agresivas.

hint.es: Busca la expresión que dice lo mismo que fired, pero con delicadeza.

origin.text: Mia wants to tell a friend that Sara lost her job at the bank last week. She would like to sound kind, not blunt.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mi tío está entre trabajos ahora mismo.»

feedback.es: Between jobs es el eufemismo fijo: siempre con el plural jobs.

hint.es: Es el plural de la palabra que significa «empleo».

origin.text: My uncle lost his job in March. He never says he is unemployed; he says he is between ___ right now.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mi abuela falleció el año pasado.»

answer.text: My grandmother passed away last year
accepted: My grandmother passed away last year
Last year my grandmother passed away

feedback.es: Passed away es un verbo frasal de una sola unidad: el sujeto va antes y el tiempo al final.

hint.es: El verbo con away va justo después del sujeto.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con lo que quiere decir en realidad.

pairs: We had to let him go.
She is between jobs at the moment.

pairs.es: está sin empleo, dicho con tacto

pairs: Your work is not the best, I'm afraid.

feedback.es: Cada eufemismo cambia la palabra cruda (fire, unemployed, bad, die) por otra que protege los sentimientos.

pairs: We had to let him go.
She is between jobs at the moment.

pairs.es: está sin empleo, dicho con tacto

pairs: Your work is not the best, I'm afraid.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué efecto buscaba la directora con sus palabras.

choices.text: To soften the news without changing what was really happening.
To keep from the team the fact that some colleagues were leaving.
To blame the colleagues for the difficult year.

feedback.es: Nadie duda de lo ocurrido: los eufemismos suavizan la forma de la noticia, no su contenido.

origin.audio: Last Friday our manager called the whole team together. She began gently: As you know, the company has had a difficult year, and I'm afraid we have to let three colleagues go. She never said fired, and she never said the word unemployed either. Afterwards Mia told me that her brother is between jobs too, and that he hates that word. I think the manager chose her words carefully, although nobody was in any doubt about what had happened.

prompt.es: Completa: «Decir «desempleado» a un amigo puede sonar demasiado brusco.»

feedback.es: Blunt describe la palabra directa que no protege los sentimientos del oyente.

origin.text: Saying «unemployed» to a friend who has just lost his job may sound too ___. Many people say «between jobs» instead.

prompt.es: ¿Qué opina realmente el jefe de la presentación?

choices.text: He thinks it was very good and wants only a shorter ending.
He thinks it was poor, but he says so gently.
He has not yet decided what he thinks of it.

feedback.es: «Not the best» es una atenuación: dice menos de lo que siente, y la oferta de ayuda confirma que hay algo que mejorar.

origin.text: Thank you for your presentation, Leo. It was not the best I have seen this year, and I wonder whether the ending could be a little shorter next time. Do let me know if you would like some help.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué da a entender «his health had not been the best»?

choices.text: That he had recovered well during that week.
That the doctors had made a mistake.
That he had been very ill for some time.

feedback.es: La atenuación «not the best» para la salud de un anciano indica una enfermedad larga y grave, dicha con delicadeza.

origin.audio: Hello, Mrs Clarke. I'm calling about your father. I'm afraid he passed away this morning. He was elderly, and his health had not been the best for a while, but the family was with him, and he was not in any pain.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los agentes inmobiliarios llaman «acogedor» a un piso muy pequeño.»

feedback.es: Cosy es el eufemismo inmobiliario clásico: suena agradable, pero el mensaje real es «muy pequeño».

origin.text: Estate agents rarely say «tiny». They call a very small flat «___», which is a typical euphemism.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por desgracia, tuvimos que despedir a tres personas.»

answer.text: Sadly we had to let three people go

feedback.es: Let + persona + go separa la expresión: los tres trabajadores se colocan entre let y go.

prompt.es: ¿Por qué el autor escribe «passed away» y no «died»?

choices.text: To show respect and kindness towards a family that is sad.
To keep from the family the fact that the man has really died.
To report the news more quickly and more directly.

feedback.es: En un mensaje de pésame, passed away muestra respeto y cariño; no oculta la muerte, solo la dice con delicadeza.

origin.text: Dear Mrs Kaur, we were very sad to hear that your father passed away last week. He was a kind elderly man, and he will be missed by everyone on the street. If there is anything we can do, please ask.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina realmente el hablante sobre la comida.

choices.text: It was very good, although the service was slow.
It was quite bad, although he says so gently.
It was normal, so he will go back soon.

feedback.es: La atenuación not the best y la decisión de cocinar en casa revelan que la comida decepcionó.

origin.audio: We went to the new restaurant on Saturday. The service was friendly and the room was lovely, but the food, well, let's say it was not the best I have had this year. I think I will cook at home for a while.

prompt.es: Completa: «Leo preguntó si el señor mayor había fallecido.»

feedback.es: Las preguntas de sí o no transmitidas llevan whether o if, con el sujeto antes del verbo.

origin.text: Leo was worried about the old man next door. He asked Sara ___ the elderly man had passed away, but she said he was only in hospital.

es: Identificar atenuadores (it seems, a bit, slightly, might, I wonder if, I'd suggest) en una consulta médica y entender qué mensaje real esconden.

vocabulary.es: decir con todas las letras, explicitar

teaching.en: It seems that your blood pressure is slightly higher than we would like, although the other results are perfectly normal.
teaching.es: Parece que tu presión arterial es algo más alta de lo que querríamos, aunque el resto de los resultados son perfectamente normales.
teaching.explanationEs: It seems that y slightly suavizan la noticia: el mensaje real es «tienes la tensión alta».
segments: It seems that your blood pressure is slightly higher than
we would like, although the other results are perfectly normal.
teaching.audioText: It seems that your blood pressure is slightly higher than we would like, although the other results are perfectly normal.

teaching.en: Doctors often break the news in stages and downplay it with phrases such as a bit worrying, so a patient must learn to read between the lines.
teaching.es: Los médicos suelen dar la noticia por etapas y restarle importancia con frases como a bit worrying, así que el paciente debe aprender a leer entre líneas.
teaching.explanationEs: Break the news = comunicar algo difícil; downplay = restar importancia; read between the lines = entender lo no dicho.
segments: Doctors often break the news in stages and downplay it with phrases such as
a bit worrying, so a patient must learn to read between the lines.
teaching.audioText: Doctors often break the news in stages and downplay it with phrases such as a bit worrying, so a patient must learn to read between the lines.

teaching.en: I wonder if we could try a different medicine is not really a question; it is a polite way of telling the patient what the doctor plans to do.
teaching.es: I wonder if we could try a different medicine no es realmente una pregunta: es una forma cortés de decir al paciente lo que el médico piensa hacer.
teaching.explanationEs: I wonder if + could: parece una duda, pero el médico suele proponer un cambio.
segments: I wonder if we could try a different medicine is not really a question; it
is a polite way of telling the patient what the doctor plans to do.
teaching.audioText: I wonder if we could try a different medicine is not really a question; it is a polite way of telling the patient what the doctor plans to do.

teaching.en: When a doctor says I'd suggest you rest for a week, she will not spell out that it is an order, but she is giving an instruction in a gentle voice.
teaching.es: Cuando una doctora dice I'd suggest you rest for a week, no te dirá con todas las letras que es una orden, pero da una instrucción con voz suave.
teaching.explanationEs: I'd suggest suena amable, pero el médico espera que lo hagas; spell out = decir explícitamente.
segments: When a doctor says I'd suggest you rest for a week, she will not spell out
that it is an order, but she is giving an instruction in a gentle voice.
teaching.audioText: When a doctor says I'd suggest you rest for a week, she will not spell out that it is an order, but she is giving an instruction in a gentle voice.

teaching.en: You should hedge carefully in a report: might, it seems and a little let you describe uncertain results without sounding careless.
teaching.es: Debes atenuar con cuidado en un informe: might, it seems y a little permiten describir resultados inciertos sin parecer descuidado.
teaching.explanationEs: Hedge = protegerse con matices; los atenuadores expresan el grado de certeza real.
segments: You should hedge carefully in a report: might, it seems and
a little let you describe uncertain results without sounding careless.
teaching.audioText: You should hedge carefully in a report: might, it seems and a little let you describe uncertain results without sounding careless.

teaching.en: The patient might need a second test next week: in a consultation, might usually means that the test is already being arranged.
teaching.es: Puede que el paciente necesite una segunda prueba la semana próxima: en una consulta, might suele significar que la prueba ya se está organizando.
teaching.explanationEs: Might suaviza: en una consulta suele significar que hay que hacerla.
segments: The patient might need a second test next week: in a
consultation, might usually means that the test is already being arranged.
teaching.audioText: The patient might need a second test next week: in a consultation, might usually means that the test is already being arranged.

prompt.es: ¿Qué mensaje real esconde la frase de la doctora?

choices.text: There is a real problem, but it can be treated.
There is no problem at all, so there is no need to come back.
The doctor is unsure whether the results are correct.

feedback.es: Quitados los atenuadores, queda una noticia real (hay un problema) junto con una promesa de tratamiento.

hint.es: Quita it seems y small: ¿qué noticia queda?

origin.text: Doctor: “It seems there is a small problem with your results, but nothing we cannot manage together.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Me pregunto si podríamos hacer otro análisis de sangre el viernes.»

feedback.es: I wonder if + could es la fórmula indirecta con la que el médico propone una prueba que quiere hacer.

origin.text: The results are not clear yet. I ___ if we could do another blood test on Friday.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Parece que tu presión arterial está un poco alta.»

answer.text: It seems that your blood pressure is slightly high

feedback.es: It seems that abre la noticia y slightly rebaja el adjetivo high sin ocultar el problema.

hint.es: Empieza con it seems that y termina con el adjetivo.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada atenuador con el mensaje real del médico.

pairs: I wonder if you could wait.

feedback.es: Cada atenuador rebaja el tono, pero el mensaje real sigue: un valor alto, una preocupación, una orden o una petición.

pairs: I wonder if you could wait.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la hija insistió en acompañar a su padre.

choices.text: She thought the doctor had made a mistake with the results.
She understood the doctor was more worried than her words suggested.
She wanted to ask the doctor for a different medicine.

feedback.es: La hija leyó entre líneas: tanta suavización indicaba que la preocupación era mayor de lo que decían las palabras.

origin.audio: After the tests, Dr Sara sat down with Mr Lopez and said: It seems your blood pressure is slightly high, and the results are a bit worrying, to be honest. I'd suggest you drink less coffee, and I wonder if you could come back on Friday for another test. Mr Lopez smiled with relief, thinking it was nothing. His daughter, who had read between the lines, noticed that the doctor had softened every single sentence, and she insisted on coming with him.

prompt.es: Completa: «La doctora optó por restar importancia a la noticia.»

feedback.es: Downplay describe rebajar la importancia de algo: la doctora no miente, pero lo presenta como menos grave.

origin.text: The doctor did not want to alarm him, so she chose to ___ the news by saying that the results were only a bit worrying.

prompt.es: ¿Qué espera realmente la doctora de la paciente?

choices.text: That she waits a month without doing anything different.
That she feels safe and forgets about the matter.
That she changes her food and books a visit soon.

feedback.es: Tras «might be a good idea» y «I wonder whether» hay dos instrucciones reales: comer menos azúcar y volver pronto.

origin.text: Doctor: “It might be a good idea to eat less sugar, and I wonder whether we could arrange another visit next month. There is no need to worry, but let's not leave it too long.”

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué da a entender el médico con su última frase?

choices.text: That the matter is serious enough to take seriously, without alarming him.
That the matter is so serious that he should be very afraid.
That the matter is so small that he can ignore the test.

feedback.es: La doble negación equilibra tranquilidad y aviso: no hay que asustarse, pero tampoco ignorar el problema.

origin.audio: Good morning, Mr Reed. The results are slightly unusual, and there may be something we need to look at more closely. I'd suggest another test on Monday to be sure. I wouldn't want you to worry before we know more, but I also wouldn't want you to ignore this.

prompt.es: Completa: «Te aconsejaría que descansaras unos días, aunque decides tú.»

feedback.es: I'd suggest that… es una recomendación amable que, en boca de un médico, equivale a una instrucción.

origin.text: I'd ___ that you rest for a few days, although of course the decision is yours. It might help your results.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Puede que el paciente necesite una segunda prueba.»

answer.text: The patient might need a second test

feedback.es: Might + verbo base suaviza la necesidad: en una consulta suele significar que conviene hacerla.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pide realmente el paciente con la última frase de su carta?

choices.text: That the doctor cancels the second test he has suggested.
That the doctor stops softening the news and speaks clearly.
That the doctor sends him the results of the first test.

feedback.es: El paciente ha leído los atenuadores y pide un mensaje claro: quiere saber si debe preocuparse de verdad.

origin.text: Dear Dr Lane, thank you for your message. I understand that the results are slightly unusual and that you would suggest another test. I would be grateful if you could tell me clearly whether I should be worried.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el mensaje real del médico.

choices.text: The result is fine, and the medicine is only to be safe.
The result is bad, and there is nothing more to be done.
The result is bad, treatment is needed, and it can be managed.

feedback.es: No the best y I'm afraid anuncian mala noticia; la oferta del lunes y «we can manage» indican que hay tratamiento.

origin.audio: To be honest, the result is not the best, and I'm afraid we need to start the medicine soon. I wonder if you could come in on Monday, so that we can explain how to take it. It is important, but it is something we can manage.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su presión parece estar algo baja, así que la enfermera la revisará otra vez.»

feedback.es: Seems to be + adjetivo presenta la noticia con distancia y es un atenuador típico de la consulta.

origin.text: Her blood pressure ___ to be slightly low, so the nurse will check it again in an hour.

title.es: Dar una mala noticia con tacto

es: Rechazar con tacto la propuesta de un amigo: reconocer la idea, decir que no con claridad, usar tres atenuadores y ofrecer una alternativa concreta.

teaching.en: Honestly, I'm a bit worried about the budget for this trip, because money is rather tight after the holidays.
teaching.es: La verdad es que me preocupa un poco el presupuesto de este viaje, porque el dinero anda bastante justo después de las vacaciones.
teaching.explanationEs: Honestly y a bit son atenuadores: das el motivo sin atacar la idea del otro.
segments: Honestly, I'm a bit worried about the budget for this
trip, because money is rather tight after the holidays.
teaching.audioText: Honestly, I'm a bit worried about the budget for this trip, because money is rather tight after the holidays.

teaching.en: I'm afraid I can't say yes to your proposal this time, although I really appreciate you thinking of me.
teaching.es: Me temo que no puedo decir que sí a tu propuesta esta vez, aunque te agradezco mucho que hayas pensado en mí.
teaching.explanationEs: I'm afraid + can't: el rechazo es claro, pero cortés; además se agradece la propuesta.
segments: I'm afraid I can't say yes to your proposal this
time, although I really appreciate you thinking of me.
teaching.audioText: I'm afraid I can't say yes to your proposal this time, although I really appreciate you thinking of me.

teaching.en: Perhaps it would be better to wait until the budget is less tight; that way nobody feels let down if the plan has to change.
teaching.es: Quizá sería mejor esperar a que el presupuesto esté menos ajustado; así nadie se siente decepcionado si hay que cambiar el plan.
teaching.explanationEs: Perhaps + would be better: sugerencia suave que a la vez frena el plan; let down = decepcionar.
segments: Perhaps it would be better to wait until the budget is less tight;
that way nobody feels let down if the plan has to change.
teaching.audioText: Perhaps it would be better to wait until the budget is less tight; that way nobody feels let down if the plan has to change.

teaching.en: How about a cheaper alternative, such as a day trip instead? Suggesting something concrete shows that you are being tactful, not just negative.
teaching.es: ¿Qué tal una alternativa más barata, como una excursión de un día? Proponer algo concreto demuestra que eres diplomático y no solo negativo.
teaching.explanationEs: Un rechazo sin alternativa deja al otro con las manos vacías; How about… instead? la ofrece.
segments: How about a cheaper alternative, such as a day trip instead? Suggesting
something concrete shows that you are being tactful, not just negative.
teaching.audioText: How about a cheaper alternative, such as a day trip instead? Suggesting something concrete shows that you are being tactful, not just negative.

teaching.en: It's a great proposal, but I'd rather do something smaller this time, so please let me take a rain check on the weekend away.
teaching.es: Es una gran propuesta, pero preferiría hacer algo más pequeño esta vez, así que déjame dejarlo para otra ocasión.
teaching.explanationEs: I'd rather + verbo base = preferencia suave; take a rain check = aplazar sin cerrar la puerta.
segments: It's a great proposal, but I'd rather do something smaller this time,
so please let me take a rain check on the weekend away.
teaching.audioText: It's a great proposal, but I'd rather do something smaller this time, so please let me take a rain check on the weekend away.

teaching.en: A refusal works best in four steps: acknowledge the idea, say no clearly, explain honestly and offer an alternative.
teaching.es: Un rechazo funciona mejor en cuatro pasos: reconocer la idea, decir que no con claridad, explicar con sinceridad y ofrecer una alternativa.
teaching.explanationEs: Tres atenuadores bastan: con más, el «no» se pierde.
segments: A refusal works best in four steps: acknowledge the idea,
say no clearly, explain honestly and offer an alternative.
teaching.audioText: A refusal works best in four steps: acknowledge the idea, say no clearly, explain honestly and offer an alternative.

prompt.es: Elige el rechazo claro pero cortés a la invitación de Sara.

choices.text: It's a lovely idea, Sara. Perhaps I might possibly be able to come, but I honestly don't know yet.
It's a lovely idea, Sara, but I'm afraid I can't this time. How about a day trip instead?
No, thanks, Sara. A weekend at the coast is far too expensive for me this month.

feedback.es: Reconoce la idea, dice no con claridad y ofrece una alternativa; las otras respuestas son vagas o bruscas.

hint.es: Busca la frase que dice no con claridad y ofrece algo a cambio.

origin.text: Sara has invited you to spend a weekend at the coast. You love the idea, but your budget is very tight this month.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me temo que el presupuesto está muy ajustado este mes.»

feedback.es: Tight budget es la colocación para un presupuesto muy ajustado; además evita decir «no tengo dinero».

origin.text: I'd love to see the exhibition with you, but I'm afraid the budget is ___ this month. Could we go next month instead?

prompt.es: Ordena: «Prefiero hacer algo más pequeño esta vez.»

answer.text: I'd rather do something smaller this time
accepted: I'd rather do something smaller this time
This time I'd rather do something smaller

feedback.es: I'd rather va seguido de un verbo base sin to: I'd rather do.

hint.es: Empieza con I'd rather y sigue con un verbo base.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la pieza del no amable que cumple.

pairs: I'm afraid I can't this time.

feedback.es: Cada frase cubre una pieza distinta: reconocer, rechazar, justificar con suavidad u ofrecer otra cosa.

pairs: I'm afraid I can't this time.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué valoró Leo de la respuesta de su amigo.

choices.text: That the answer was a firm yes with some conditions.
That the answer was vague and left the door open.
That the answer was clear, although it was kind.

feedback.es: Leo dice que prefiere una respuesta clara a una vaga: el tacto no le molestó porque el no era inequívoco.

origin.audio: My friend Leo asked me to join his new business. I liked him and the idea, so I did not want to let him down. I said: It's a great idea, and I'm grateful that you asked me. Honestly, though, I'm a bit worried about the money, and I'm afraid I can't say yes this year. Perhaps we could start with a small project instead, and I'll take a rain check on the full business. Leo was not angry at all; he said he preferred a clear answer to a vague one.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me preocupa un poco el dinero este mes.»

feedback.es: A bit worried es un atenuador: muestra preocupación real sin dramatizar.

origin.text: Thanks for the invitation, but I'm afraid I must say no. Honestly, I'm a bit ___ about the money this month.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender realmente la respuesta a la propuesta de Leo?

choices.text: That he likes the flat, but the price makes him refuse.
That he is very happy and will sign the contract next week.
That he dislikes the proposal and wants to end the idea.

feedback.es: La respuesta alaba la idea y usa «rather more than I can manage» como atenuación de un rechazo real por el precio.

origin.text: Leo proposes that you both move to a bigger flat in June. You reply: That sounds exciting, and I would love to live closer to you. Honestly, though, the rent is rather more than I can manage at the moment.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿con qué propósito dice la hablante «I'll take a rain check»?

choices.text: To cancel the plan for ever without saying so.
To keep the plan open for another day.
To ask the listener to choose a date alone.

feedback.es: Take a rain check deja la puerta abierta: no cancela el plan, lo aplaza para otra ocasión.

origin.audio: It's a lovely plan, but I'm afraid I'm busy on Friday. Honestly, I've been working late all week, and I'd rather rest. Could we go on Sunday instead? If that doesn't work, I'll take a rain check.

prompt.es: Completa: «No quiero decepcionarte, así que seré sincera.»

feedback.es: Let someone down significa decepcionar o fallar a alguien; por eso se dice que no con sinceridad.

origin.text: I don't want to let you ___, so let me be honest: I'm afraid I can't join the project this year.

prompt.es: Escribe el mensaje: reconoce la idea, rechaza, da el motivo y ofrece una alternativa.

answer.text: Hi Mia, thank you for the invitation. It's a great idea, and I can see why you like it. Honestly, I'm a bit worried about this month: I have exams, and my time is very tight. I'm afraid I can't say yes to a film club every Friday, because I wouldn't be a good host and I don't want to let you down. Perhaps it would be better to wait until the exams are over. How about a film evening once a month instead? We could watch a film at your place next Saturday and then decide together. I'd rather do something small for now, and I would love to take a rain check on the weekly club. I hope you understand! See you soon, Ana
accepted: Hi Mia, thank you for the invitation. It's a great idea, and I can see why you like it. Honestly, I'm a bit worried about this month: I have exams, and my time is very tight. I'm afraid I can't say yes to a film club every Friday, because I wouldn't be a good host and I don't want to let you down. Perhaps it would be better to wait until the exams are over. How about a film evening once a month instead? We could watch a film at your place next Saturday and then decide together. I'd rather do something small for now, and I would love to take a rain check on the weekly club. I hope you understand! See you soon, Ana

Hello Mia, thanks for thinking of me. A film club is a nice idea. To be honest, I'm a little tired this month, and the exams are very close. I'm afraid I can't join every Friday, because I need that time to study. Maybe we could start in June, when my exams are finished. What if we watch one film together this Saturday instead? I would bring the snacks and you could choose the film. It would be fun, and we could decide about the club later. I'd rather be honest than say yes and cancel at the last minute. Speak soon, Ana

feedback.es: El mensaje eficaz reconoce la idea, rechaza con claridad, suaviza con tres atenuadores y termina con una alternativa concreta.

origin.text: Tu amiga Mia propone organizar un club de cine todos los viernes en tu casa. Tienes exámenes y poco tiempo este mes. Escribe entre 150 y 200 palabras: reconoce su idea, rechaza con claridad, usa tres atenuadores (por ejemplo, honestly, a bit, perhaps o I'm afraid), da el motivo y propón una alternativa.

evidenceGroups: thank you for thinking of me
i am afraid i can not
i do not think i can

prompt.es: ¿Qué pretende el hablante con la última frase de su respuesta?

choices.text: To change his mind and lend the car after all.
To blame Sara for asking for such a big favour.
To soften the refusal by offering a practical alternative.

feedback.es: La oferta de llevarla a la estación no cambia el no: lo hace más amable al dar una alternativa útil.

origin.text: I'm afraid I can't lend you the car for a whole month, Sara. I need it for work, and honestly, I'd feel worried if something happened to it. I could drive you to the station on Saturdays instead, if that helps.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace la hablante con el plan de Tom.

choices.text: She declines Friday and suggests Sunday instead.
She accepts Friday without any problem at all.
She cancels the plan completely and apologises.

feedback.es: Rechaza el viernes con I'm afraid y propone el domingo: el plan sigue vivo con otra fecha.

origin.audio: Thanks so much for thinking of me, Tom. It's a lovely plan, but I'm afraid I'm busy on Friday, and I'd rather not rush it. Could we go on Sunday instead? If that doesn't work, no worries at all; we'll find another time.

prompt.es: Completa: «Prefiero quedarme en casa esta noche, si no te importa.»

feedback.es: I'd rather + verbo base expresa una preferencia suave y cortés.

origin.text: I'm exhausted after the trip. I'd ___ stay at home tonight, if you don't mind.

es: Transmitir a un tercero dos preguntas de otras personas con preguntas indirectas (asked whether, wanted to know why) y responder con diplomacia usando atenuadores y una solución.

teaching.en: I am writing on behalf of the tenants of the building, who asked me to bring up two questions about the rent and the heating.
teaching.es: Les escribo en nombre de los inquilinos del edificio, que me pidieron plantear dos preguntas sobre el alquiler y la calefacción.
teaching.explanationEs: On behalf of = en nombre de; bring up = plantear un tema; rent es el alquiler que se paga.
segments: I am writing on behalf of the tenants of the building, who asked
me to bring up two questions about the rent and the heating.
teaching.audioText: I am writing on behalf of the tenants of the building, who asked me to bring up two questions about the rent and the heating.

teaching.en: The tenant asked whether the landlord could repair the heating before Friday, and she added that the flat had been cold for a week.
teaching.es: La inquilina preguntó si el casero podía reparar la calefacción antes del viernes, y añadió que el piso llevaba una semana frío.
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta indirecta: whether + sujeto antes del verbo, sin did ni «?»; could retrocede desde can.
segments: The tenant asked whether the landlord could repair the heating before Friday,
and she added that the flat had been cold for a week.
teaching.audioText: The tenant asked whether the landlord could repair the heating before Friday, and she added that the flat had been cold for a week.

teaching.en: Mia wanted to know why the rent had gone up this year, and Tom wondered whether he could pay it a week late.
teaching.es: Mia quería saber por qué había subido el alquiler este año, y Tom se preguntaba si podría pagarlo con una semana de retraso.
teaching.explanationEs: Wanted to know + why + sujeto + verbo: sin inversión; had gone up retrocede un tiempo.
segments: Mia wanted to know why the rent had gone up this year,
and Tom wondered whether he could pay it a week late.
teaching.audioText: Mia wanted to know why the rent had gone up this year, and Tom wondered whether he could pay it a week late.

teaching.en: To report a question, put the subject before the verb and use if or whether: she asked whether it would take long, never whether would it take long.
teaching.es: Para transmitir una pregunta, pon el sujeto antes del verbo y usa if o whether: preguntó si tardaría mucho, nunca whether would it take long.
teaching.explanationEs: Las preguntas de sí o no llevan if o whether; las de why, when o what conservan su palabra.
segments: To report a question, put the subject before the verb and use if or
whether: she asked whether it would take long, never whether would it take long.
teaching.audioText: To report a question, put the subject before the verb and use if or whether: she asked whether it would take long, never whether would it take long.

teaching.en: I'd like to reply to both questions, if I may, and I hope my answer will help to get across that we take the concerns of every tenant seriously.
teaching.es: Me gustaría responder a las dos preguntas, si me lo permite, y espero que mi respuesta ayude a transmitir que nos tomamos en serio las preocupaciones de cada inquilino.
teaching.explanationEs: If I may suaviza el turno de palabra; get across = lograr que el mensaje llegue.
segments: I'd like to reply to both questions, if I may, and I hope my answer
will help to get across that we take the concerns of every tenant seriously.
teaching.audioText: I'd like to reply to both questions, if I may, and I hope my answer will help to get across that we take the concerns of every tenant seriously.

teaching.en: That was a diplomatic reply: she said no gently, explained the reason honestly and offered the tenants a practical solution.
teaching.es: Fue una respuesta diplomática: dijo que no con delicadeza, explicó el motivo con sinceridad y ofreció a los inquilinos una solución práctica.
teaching.explanationEs: Diplomatic = con tacto: rechazo cortés más una solución.
segments: That was a diplomatic reply: she said no gently, explained
the reason honestly and offered the tenants a practical solution.
teaching.audioText: That was a diplomatic reply: she said no gently, explained the reason honestly and offered the tenants a practical solution.

prompt.es: Elige cómo transmite Leo la pregunta que Tom hizo al casero.

choices.text: Tom asked whether could the landlord repair the front door that week.
Tom asked whether the landlord repaired the front door that week.
Tom asked whether the landlord could repair the front door that week.

feedback.es: La pregunta indirecta lleva whether, el sujeto antes del verbo y could en lugar de can.

hint.es: Pon el sujeto antes del verbo y cambia can por could.

origin.text: At the tenants' meeting, Tom asked the landlord directly: “Can you repair the front door this week?” Now Leo is reporting the question to Sara, who was not there.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sara quería saber por qué la calefacción estaba apagada desde el lunes.»

feedback.es: Wanted to know + why transmite la pregunta con sujeto y verbo en orden afirmativo.

hint.es: Es el verbo que significa «saber» y sigue a wanted to.

origin.text: Sara wanted to ___ why the heating had been off since Monday, but nobody in the building could tell her.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Tom se preguntaba si el casero respondería pronto.»

answer.text: Tom wondered whether the landlord would reply soon

feedback.es: Wondered whether introduce una pregunta suave y distante: el sujeto va antes de would reply.

hint.es: Empieza con Tom wondered whether y termina con soon.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fórmula con su significado al transmitir mensajes.

feedback.es: Cada fórmula cumple una función: hablar por otros, transmitir un porqué, transmitir un sí o no o sacar un tema.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué prometió el casero al final de la reunión.

choices.text: To answer both questions in writing by Monday.
To repair the heating before the end of the week.
To lower the rent for all the tenants next year.

feedback.es: El casero no resuelve nada todavía: promete responder por escrito el lunes a las dos preguntas.

origin.audio: Leo had been chosen to speak on behalf of the tenants, and he was nervous. At the meeting he told the landlord: Two people asked me to bring up something. Tom wanted to know whether the heating could be repaired before Friday, and Mia wondered why the rent had gone up again this year. The landlord looked at him for a moment and said that he would reply to both questions in writing by Monday. Leo thanked him and sat down, happy that he had got the message across without sounding angry.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tom se preguntaba si podría pagar el alquiler con una semana de retraso.»

feedback.es: Las preguntas de sí o no transmitidas con wondered se introducen con whether o if.

origin.text: Mia asked why the rent had gone up this year, and Tom wondered ___ he could pay it a week late.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la versión correcta al transmitir la pregunta de Mia?

choices.text: Mia wanted to know why hadn't the landlord answered her message.
Mia wanted to know why the landlord hadn't answered her message.
Mia wanted to know why the landlord hasn't answered my message.

feedback.es: La versión correcta conserva why, pone el sujeto antes del verbo y retrocede un tiempo cambiando my por her.

origin.text: Mia was angry. She said to Leo: “Why hasn't the landlord answered my message? I sent it three days ago, and the heating is still broken!” Leo now tells Sara what Mia asked.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué actitud muestra la casera al abrir con «I wonder if…»?

choices.text: She is unsure: she does not know how to fix the heating.
She is annoyed: she wants to end the discussion quickly.
She is open: she invites them to look for a solution together.

feedback.es: I wonder if we could… funciona como una invitación a cooperar, no como una duda real.

origin.audio: I understand your concern, and I wonder if we could find a solution together. The repair will start on Thursday, but I'm afraid the rent cannot change this year.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿qué decide finalmente la casera?

choices.text: She accepts the repair but refuses to lower the rent.
She refuses the repair and promises to lower the rent.
She agrees to both requests without any conditions.

feedback.es: La reparación empieza el jueves, pero el alquiler no cambia este año: acepta una petición y rechaza otra.

origin.audio: I understand your concern, and I wonder if we could find a solution together. The repair will start on Thursday, but I'm afraid the rent cannot change this year.

prompt.es: Escribe el mensaje a la casera: transmite las dos preguntas y responde con tacto.

answer.text: Dear Sara, thank you for your message. I understand that some tenants have paid the rent late, and I wonder if we could find a simple solution together. Honestly, I think the start of the month is a bit difficult for some people. On behalf of the flat, I would like to pass on two questions. Tom asked whether you could repair the heating before Friday, because it seems to be getting colder. Mia wanted to know why the rent had gone up this year. I'm afraid I can't answer that myself, so I would be grateful for your reply. Perhaps we could agree on one payment date each month instead, and everybody would know what to expect. I hope this is fine for you, and I would like to thank you in advance for your help. Best wishes, Leo
accepted: Dear Sara, thank you for your message. I understand that some tenants have paid the rent late, and I wonder if we could find a simple solution together. Honestly, I think the start of the month is a bit difficult for some people. On behalf of the flat, I would like to pass on two questions. Tom asked whether you could repair the heating before Friday, because it seems to be getting colder. Mia wanted to know why the rent had gone up this year. I'm afraid I can't answer that myself, so I would be grateful for your reply. Perhaps we could agree on one payment date each month instead, and everybody would know what to expect. I hope this is fine for you, and I would like to thank you in advance for your help. Best wishes, Leo

Hello Sara, thank you for writing. I'm sorry that some rent has arrived late, and I wonder if a fixed date could help everyone. It might be a bit hard for people to pay on the first day. I have two questions from my flatmates. Tom wondered whether the heating could be repaired before Friday, since it seems to be getting colder every night. Mia asked why the rent had gone up this year, and she would like to hear your reply. I'd suggest that we talk about both points on Saturday, if that is convenient. What if we agree on a fixed date each month instead? Thank you for your patience, and I hope we can find a fair answer. Kind regards, Leo

feedback.es: El mensaje diplomático transmite las dos preguntas con orden afirmativo, suaviza la respuesta con atenuadores y termina con una solución.

origin.text: Eres el representante de un piso compartido. La casera, Sara, te escribió: «Algunos inquilinos pagan tarde.» Tom preguntó si ella podía arreglar la calefacción antes del viernes, y Mia quiso saber por qué subió el alquiler este año. Escribe entre 170 y 220 palabras: transmite las dos preguntas con estructuras indirectas, responde a la queja con al menos dos atenuadores y propón una solución.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo transmite Ana la pregunta de Carlos a una vecina?

choices.text: Carlos wanted to know when will the landlord fix the window.
Carlos wanted to know when the landlord would fix the window.
Carlos wanted to know when you will fix the window.

feedback.es: Se conserva when, el sujeto va antes del verbo y will retrocede a would; you pasa a the landlord.

origin.text: Carlos was tired of waiting. He wrote to the landlord: “When will you fix the window? It has been broken since Monday, and the rain is coming in.” His flatmate Ana now tells a neighbour what he asked.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el mensaje real detrás de los atenuadores.

choices.text: The rent will go down, and she wants to arrange a meeting.
The weekend meeting is cancelled, so nothing will change.
The rent will rise, and she wants him to tell the tenants.

feedback.es: It seems… a bit anuncia la subida, y I wonder if you could let… know es una petición real de avisar a los demás.

origin.audio: I'm sorry to say this, but it seems the rent will go up a bit next year. Perhaps we could talk about it at the weekend, and I wonder if you could let the other tenants know in the meantime.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mia se preguntaba por qué el casero no había respondido.»

answer.text: Mia wondered why the landlord had not replied

feedback.es: Wondered why + sujeto + had not replied: sin inversión y con el verbo un tiempo atrás.
